title: Discharge the Nat.find Existence Proof to Make F_k(N,ℓ) Genuinely Well-Defined

problemStatement.formal: F(k, N, \ell) := \operatorname{Nat.find}(\texttt{supersaturation\_exists}\ k\ N\ \ell), \text{ where } \exists\, M \in \mathbb{N},\ \forall A \subseteq \mathbb{N} \text{ with } |A| = N,\ \operatorname{countAPs}(A, k) \ge M \Rightarrow \operatorname{ContainsAP}(A, \ell). \text{ Prove this existential without sorry; the witness } M = \binom{N}{k} + 1 \text{ works vacuously via } \operatorname{countAPs}(A,k) \le \binom{|A|}{k}.
problemStatement.plain: The parent formalization defines a supersaturation function F_k(N, ℓ) using Nat.find, which needs a proof that some finite threshold M exists such that any size-N set with at least M many k-term arithmetic progressions must contain an ℓ-term one. The parent supplies a placeholder witness M = N² + 1 and leaves the required implication as a sorry. This question asks whether that existence proof can be completed. Crucially, the placeholder N² + 1 is the wrong number for k ≥ 3 (a size-N set can have up to C(N, k) many k-APs, exceeding N²), so the sorry cannot be closed with it. Using the correct witness M = C(N, k) + 1 makes the hypothesis impossible — hence the implication vacuously true — and closes the gap honestly using the already-proven bound countAPs A k ≤ C(|A|, k).
whyMatters: Removes a sorry and makes F_k(N, ℓ) a genuinely well-defined natural number rather than Nat.find applied to an unproven proposition.
Fixes a latent correctness bug: the placeholder witness N² + 1 is mathematically false for k ≥ 3; the honest threshold is C(N, k).
Cleanly separates the elementary (existence of a finite threshold) from the deep (the quantitative Fox–Pohoata value F_k(N, ℓ) = N^{2-o(1)}).
